CLIP SHRINKER CHANGELOG
=======================
Made with Claude (Anthropic) by Vergil. Open source under MIT, see LICENSE.txt.
Newest version first.


2.7.5
- HDR clips whose height does not shrink evenly (like PS5 recordings, 1920x1088 .webm) showed no thumbnails
  on the timeline. They do now. Exports of such clips were not affected.
- A clip's title bar shows the file name (bold) on one line and the video's data and length after editing
  under it, with the same spacing from the edge on both sides.
- Mouse pointers: the left-right arrow over the trim handles and the edges of effect sections and sounds,
  a pointing hand over effect headers, sounds and the effect / sound buttons, and a closed hand while one of
  them is dragged.


2.7.0
- New module "Sound track": put your own sound files on a Sounds lane under each clip's timeline. Drop sound
  files on the lane, or open the new "Sounds" list (next to Transition): its green sounds, each with its
  waveform, can be dragged onto a clip's lane, or added at the playhead with their + (A adds the highlighted
  one). Drag a sound to move it, drag its ends to trim it; right-click, Delete or Backspace removes it. A
  selected sound has its own volume (-20 to +20 dB) and fade in / out. Sounds keep their normal speed inside
  speed sections, play in the preview, are mixed into the clip's first audio track in the export (a clip
  without sound gets a track for them), and are saved with projects and the session; a missing sound file is
  listed when a project opens. Undo covers all of it. A limiter after the mix keeps loud sounds over loud game
  audio from clipping.
- The library is the folder modules\sound-track\sounds (created at start-up): "Add files..." copies sound
  files there, "Open folder" opens it, and each sound in the list has a play button to listen to it. Drag the
  grip at the bottom of the list to make it longer or shorter.
- Not in this version yet: lowering the game sound while a sound plays (ducking).
- "Plugins" are now called "modules" (the Modules button, window and folder), because they are parts of the
  program you switch on and off, not add-ons you install. The "plugins" folder of an older version is moved
  into "modules" at the first start, with RIFE and your sounds; your on / off switches are kept.


2.6.0
- Exports work without an NVIDIA card. Besides NVENC, Clip Shrinker can now encode on AMD (AMF) and Intel
  (Quick Sync) graphics, and with Windows' own encoder (Media Foundation), on the graphics card or, as a last
  resort, on the CPU (H.264 only, slower). At start-up a short test encode checks which ones work on the PC,
  and the Codec list shows only those. A codec from settings or a project that this PC cannot run switches to
  the closest one that works (HEVC stays HEVC when possible). NVENC exports are unchanged. AMD and Intel are
  untested so far (no such card was at hand): please report the log if their file sizes land far off.
- PCs without NVIDIA decoding (CUDA) now decode on the CPU from the start, in the preview and the export,
  instead of failing first and retrying.
- New plugin "Sound equalizer": five bands (60 Hz, 250 Hz, 1 kHz, 4 kHz, 12 kHz; -12 to
  +12 dB) and Volume (-20 to +20 dB) on a card over the preview, opened with the equalizer button next to the
  sun button (also in full screen). Values can be dragged or typed (3, +3 dB, -6dB; Enter confirms). Heard in
  the preview, used on every audio track of the export, saved with projects. A limiter catches peaks when
  something is boosted. Only one of the Picture and Equalizer cards is open at a time.
- Top bar: a notice left of "Plugins" shows "GPU Encoding is ON" (green) when the chosen codec encodes on the
  graphics card, or "GPU Encoding is OFF" (orange) when it runs on the CPU. Hovering it lists the encoders that
  work on the PC and whether GPU decoding and GPU denoise work (handy for bug reports).
- Resolution: the 75% option is replaced by 4K, 1440p, 1080p and 720p (the picture is made that high, never
  larger than the clip). {res} in file names follows (an export at 2160 lines is named 4K). A 75% setting
  saved by an older version falls back to the default.
- Audio: "Original" in "Bitrate per track" keeps the clips' own audio bitrate (raised to the next AAC step,
  at most 320k; 192k when a clip does not report one). "Keep separate tracks" is now "Keep as separate
  tracks" (older settings and projects are read as before).
- Codec: the Windows CPU encoder is only listed when no graphics card encoder works. In the open list each
  codec has a short hint under its name, e.g. "- recommended for your NVIDIA GPU" or "- Windows encoder,
  lower quality", so it is clear which one to pick.
- Export panel wording: "ignored if empty" next to Bitrate, "Export folder"
  (was "Save folder") with the hint "Asks at export when empty.", and a new hint above the dynamic label
  buttons.
- The effect buttons read "Speed Up | S", "Slow Down | D", "Zoom | Z" (with the current hotkeys).
- Plugins window: a changelog opens across the whole card, and the scroll bar sits beside the cards instead
  of over them.
- Every built-in plugin is on after the first start, so new users see all features. Switches set in an
  earlier version are kept.
- About window: a line next to the GitHub link checks for a newer release when the window opens (blinking
  green while checking, then "You have the latest version" or a "Version x is available" link to the release
  page). It is only shown there: no pop-ups, nothing downloaded.
- Picture adjustments: the Denoise row is hidden when the ffmpeg in the library folder has no denoise filter
  (an older copy kept from before 2.5.0); before, exports with denoise failed there.
- The bundled ffmpeg is rebuilt with the AMD, Intel and Windows encoders and the equalizer filter. It now
  includes AMD's AMF headers and Intel's oneVPL dispatcher (both MIT, see AMF-LICENSE.txt and
  oneVPL-LICENSE.txt). It still needs no DLLs beyond the ones that come with Windows.


2.5.0
- Picture adjustments: new Denoise slider (0 to 100 %, light to strong) on the Picture card. It removes
  grain and noise from dark or low-light footage, in the preview and the export, and is saved with projects.
  It runs on the graphics card through OpenCL (any recent NVIDIA, AMD or Intel driver); without OpenCL it
  runs on the CPU, where exports get much slower. Clips that stay HDR ("Convert HDR" off) are not denoised,
  because the filter works in 8-bit. Exports with denoise take longer even on the graphics card (about 3 to
  4 times on an RTX 5070).
- Built-in plugins that came with an older version get their new plugin.json and changelog on the first start
  (Picture adjustments 1.1.0, Timeline effects 1.1.0).
- The bundled ffmpeg is rebuilt (November 2026 sources) with the denoise filters and the OpenCL loader built
  in. ffmpeg's best-known denoiser (hqdn3d) is not included: it is only allowed in GPL builds, and Clip
  Shrinker's ffmpeg stays LGPL. The OpenCL loader is Apache 2.0, see OpenCL-ICD-Loader-LICENSE.txt.
- Clip transitions are part of the app again instead of the Timeline effects plugin, so joined videos keep
  their transition with the plugin off. They moved out of the Effects window into a "Transition" drop-down
  next to the clear button (transition effect with the hover preview, and its length). The button is shown
  when 2 or more clips are in the list.
- "Clear all" is now called "Clear all clips".


2.4.0
- Plugins: a new "Plugins" button (left of About) lists the plugins with an on / off switch, their version,
  author and changelog, a red delete button and "Open plugin folder". Each plugin is a folder in plugins\ with
  a plugin.json and a CHANGELOG.txt. A deleted plugin that came with Clip Shrinker stays in the list greyed
  out, with a Restore button that downloads it again from GitHub.
- Timeline effects is now a plugin: speed up / slow motion / zoom sections, the effect buttons under the
  preview, the Effects button and window (F2), clip transitions and RIFE. Switched off, these are hidden and
  left out of the preview and the export; sections already on the clips are kept and come back with it.
  RIFE moved from library\rife into plugins\timeline-effects\rife (moved automatically on the first start).
- Bitrate presets is now a plugin: the Bitrate presets button, the preset list in the clip title bars,
  "Preset (all clips)" and the preset hotkeys. Switched off, clips export with the Export panel's size / bitrate.
- New plugin "Picture adjustments" (off by default): brightness, contrast and saturation (-100% to +100%) on a
  card over the preview, opened with the sun button next to full screen (also in full screen). Values can be
  dragged or typed (25, +25%, -40 %; Enter confirms). Used in the preview and the export, saved with projects.
  (Denoise follows in 2.5.0.)
- Export panel: the save folder has its own SAVING section under FILE NAMES, together with "Save session on
  exit" (was "Restore the last session on start" in the Effects window).
- Shortcuts window: the plugin shortcuts are at the end under "EFFECTS (plugin)" (F2 included) and are only
  listed while the Timeline effects plugin is on.


2.3.0
- New "Keep original file name" tick under Suffix, ticked by default (file names as before). Unticked, the
  clip's name is left out and only the prefix and suffix with their dynamic labels name the file, e.g.
  2026-11-15_HEVC.mp4. Files that would get the same name get " (2)", " (3)" and so on.
- The tick is greyed out (and counts as ticked) while Prefix and Suffix are both empty, since the file would
  have no name.


2.2.2
- Softer stripes over the trimmed-away parts of a timeline: 15% black in dark mode and 7% white in light mode
  instead of strong black, and they follow the Dark mode switch.
- The stripes are drawn as smooth lines that run straight off the top and bottom edges, so they no longer
  look jagged or show slanted ends.


2.2.1
- Play starts without the black flash: the preview keeps showing the current frame until the first playback
  frame is ready (ffmpeg needs about 0.2 s to seek), then switches straight to the moving picture. Also in
  full screen.
- The first play after starting the program no longer tries a GPU scaling mode the bundled ffmpeg doesn't
  have, so it starts a little sooner.


2.2.0
- The hints under the preview are now buttons: "Speed Up [S]", "Slow Down [D]" and "Zoom [Z]", in the
  colours of their sections, with the current hotkey (it follows the Shortcuts window). Click one to add the
  effect at the playhead of the active clip, or drag it by its dotted handle onto any clip's timeline to add
  it there (a dashed line shows where). The hint "Space = play / pause" is gone; it is in the Shortcuts window.
- File names: the dynamic label buttons sit above Prefix and Suffix, with a short explanation under them.
- An empty suffix no longer adds the codec name: clip.mp4 instead of clip_HEVC.mp4. Use the {codec} label to
  keep the old names. (A file that would overwrite its source gets " (2)" added.)


2.1.0
- Clip title bars are 20% taller, with a larger bitrate drop-down and buttons. "Reset zoom" is dark grey
  (white with black text in light mode); the remove button is grey with a red X (white in light mode).
- Clips that aren't selected show a 25% taller thumbnail strip.
- The trimmed-away parts of a timeline get dark slanted stripes.
- Play, sound and volume now sit on the preview (bottom left), leaving the bar under it free. While playing
  they show only when the mouse is over the preview.
- New full-screen preview: the button at the bottom right of the preview or F (can be changed in Shortcuts).
  Esc, F or a double-click leaves it; the other shortcuts keep working. If F is already used by one of your
  shortcuts or bitrate presets, full screen gets F11 instead.
- Play also works with the playhead outside the trimmed part: it plays once to the end of the video and stops
  instead of looping.
- Name fields for the prefix and suffix: {date}, {time}, {preset}, {res}, {size} and {codec} are filled in
  for each exported file. Buttons under Suffix insert them at the cursor.
- Effects window: the section headings no longer end in "effects".


2.0.0
Rewritten in C# (.NET 10, WPF) for a faster, smoother Windows interface. Exports match 1.0.8 exactly: same
ffmpeg commands, size search and file names, checked against 1.0.8 with automated tests.
- No more Python. ClipShrinker.exe is one self-contained program with .NET built in, next to the library folder
  (ffmpeg, ffprobe, RIFE). It starts faster, shows no hidden window at start-up and resizes smoothly with every
  panel visible, so the "Hide the panels while resizing" option is gone.
- Thumbnails, sound preparation and playback run on their own threads, so the window stays responsive.
- If ffmpeg is missing, the program offers the one-time download itself. Setup.bat is gone.
- New timeline look: thumbnails fill the timeline edge to edge. Speed sections get a short header band on top,
  zoom sections at the bottom, in the colour of their edge lines. Thinner edge lines, a hand cursor over
  anything draggable, rounded corners, and red "Reset zoom" and remove buttons. Clicking inside a zoom section
  selects it, as with speed sections.
- The preview zoom bracket can be dragged from anywhere inside it (move cursor).
- Every keyboard shortcut can be changed in the Shortcuts window (F1). Keys show as keycaps like in PowerToys:
  click one and press the new key. A key that's already taken says where it's used and can't be saved; "Reset"
  restores the default. Only Esc, Enter and Tab are fixed, so undo/redo, save, open, export, play, mute,
  select all and delete can now be changed too. The window also lists the mouse actions as short tips.
- Bitrate presets show and record their hotkey the same way, with lines between presets and a red delete button.
- New "Preset (all clips)" drop-down under "or Bitrate" gives every clip the same preset at once ("Auto bitrate"
  resets them all).
- Audio bitrate per track is now 128k, 192k, 256k or 320k. 48k to 96k were removed; a saved lower value
  becomes 128k.
- Loading many videos or a project shows a small window with a progress ring and counter until thumbnails are
  ready.
- Export: the progress bar moves smoothly, its text has no outline (black in light mode), and the stop button is
  red while exporting.
- Dark mode is an on/off switch at the top right. Light mode has grey clip title bars and summary panel.
- The bitrate preset list in a clip's title bar stays readable when hovered on the blue (active) title bar.
- The divider under the preview has a visible grip; the clip list's scroll bar sits on the sidebar divider.
- Fixed: the Resolution list looked empty after opening a project with a fixed bitrate.
- Settings, presets, projects (.clipproj) and the last session from 1.0.x still load.


1.0.8
- Faster first start: the NVENC check (one ffmpeg run) now happens in the background instead of holding up the
  window. On the very first start, Windows scanning the freshly unpacked Python and ffmpeg files could keep the
  window hidden for several seconds.
- Much smoother resizing: while you drag the window edge, the side panel and preview/clip list are hidden behind
  an empty panel and come back when you let go. Windows repainted every widget on each size step (about 180 ms
  with all panels, about 30 ms without), which made dragging choppy; it now runs at about 20 to 30 steps per
  second. Turn it off with "Hide the panels while resizing the window" in Effects > App.
- Timelines, the "Drop videos here" box, the "Add videos" strip and the progress bar redraw at most about 30
  times per second, and the total length is no longer recalculated on every step.
- The About window links to the GitHub project page (github.com/Vergilcd/ClipShrinker).
- Fixed: two harmless "Duplicate element DangerButton.button" errors were logged to clipshrinker.log on every
  start (the red "Clear all" style was created twice).
- clipshrinker.log now has timing lines for start-up ("[start-up ...]") and a summary after each resize
  ("[resize] ..."), only for finding slow spots.
- The license is now a plain MIT LICENSE file, so GitHub shows "MIT" again. Third-party components moved to
  THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt.

1.0.7
- Removed the developer helper Prepare-Portable-Python.bat from the package. It only prepared the bundled
  Python and isn't needed to run the program.

1.0.6
- Clicking anywhere outside a sidebar text field or drop-down now leaves it: the cursor stops blinking, typed
  values are accepted, and a chosen drop-down entry no longer stays highlighted.

1.0.5
- The note under Crop ("already narrower - no crop") is smaller and always one line, so the settings don't shift
  when it appears. The settings area also avoids repeated re-layouts when its scrollbar comes and goes (a
  possible cause of doubled-up drawing seen on one computer).

1.0.4
- The Shortcuts window uses two columns and is about half as tall (it was cut off on 1080p screens).

1.0.3
- The bundled Python is about 9 MB smaller on disk (about 3 MB smaller download). Removed: sqlite3, unittest,
  turtle, Tix, Tcl time-zone data, Tk demos and the Python self-test files.

1.0.2
- Fixed: the Project menu stayed open at its old position when the window was moved. It now closes when the
  window moves, is resized or loses focus.
- Fixed: the Shortcuts and About windows could be opened many times. Now only one of each opens; the button or
  F1 brings it to the front.

1.0.1
- Fixed: the Project menu stayed open until the Project button was clicked again. It now closes when you click
  elsewhere or switch windows.

1.0.0 (first release)
- The bottom of the Export panel (Summary, progress bar, Export button) sits on a darker panel with a thin line
  on top, with even gaps above the Summary, above the progress bar and between the bar and the Export button.
- Panel headings are now EXPORT SETTINGS and AUDIO SETTINGS.
- Fixed: the Summary text got larger after switching between dark and light mode.
- The About window is bigger and resizable. The Shortcuts window no longer shows the version.
- The changelog moved from the readme into CHANGELOG.txt (also shown in the About window).


0.9.32
- "About" button at the top right with the version, changelog, licenses and readme.

0.9.31
- The portable Python (library\python) ships with the package, so nothing needs installing or downloading.

0.9.30
- The portable Python comes from python-build-standalone (includes tkinter).

0.9.29
- The portable Python download is more reliable and writes a log (library\portable-python-log.txt).

0.9.28
- library\Prepare-Portable-Python.bat downloads the portable Python into library\python, for making a folder
  that needs no download on other PCs.

0.9.27
- Portable Python support: the program looks in library\python first. With no Python at all, setup downloads
  a portable one there (no installation, no winget).
- Clip title format: name, resolution, fps, size, original length, then length after edit.

0.9.26
- Taller thumbnails (no text line under the timeline). The clip title ends with "Length after edit". Smaller
  trim time boxes.

0.9.25
- Thumbnail order: the open clip first (using all workers), then the rest from top to bottom.

0.9.24
- Faster thumbnails (up to 8 at a time), and no gaps between thumbnails after widening the window.

0.9.23
- The film strip stays inside the grey area, with no thumbnails before the start or after the end of the video.

0.9.22
- A moved trim handle gets a time box (green left of the start handle, red right of the end handle). Type a
  time and press Enter to jump there; Esc cancels. Zoom handles can be dragged anywhere in the strip. The dark
  trimmed area reaches the thumbnail edges.

0.9.21
- Thinner trim handles with smaller flags, matching the thumbnail height. The trimmed area is darker.

0.9.20
- Trim handles have flags (triangles top and bottom). Zoom sections have handle bars and are grey until
  selected, then white. Speed and zoom handle bars are slimmer.

0.9.19
- Window title: "ClipShrinker v0.9.19", plus the project name when one is open.
- Clip title bar: "Auto bitrate" instead of "Auto", "Reset zoom" instead of "Fit", and a bigger remove (X) icon.
- The Start / End / Length line sits closer to the thumbnails.
- Fixed: the zoom bracket stayed on the preview when the playhead was outside every zoom section. It now only
  shows while the playhead is inside one.

0.9.18
- Clip timelines fill the whole card (no light or grey frame), with Start / End / Length shown inside the
  timeline at the bottom.
- Window title is just "ClipShrinker" (plus the project name). The version moved to the bottom of the
  Shortcuts window.
- A little more space between the divider and the first clip.

0.9.17
- Fixed: dragging the divider too far could push the preview over the buttons below it. The button row is now
  fixed under the preview, and the divider stops at a sensible minimum for both preview and clip list.
- The divider is back to its original thickness (the grip stays longer).

0.9.16
- Thin grey lines between sections in the Export panel, Effects window and Shortcuts window.

0.9.15
- The Play button is just a play/pause icon. The "drag the divider" hint is gone; the divider is thicker with a
  longer grip instead.
- Shortcuts, Effects, Bitrate presets and the preset editor open centred on the main window.
- "Open effect settings" (F2) can be rebound like the trim and effect keys.

0.9.14
- Preview sound: a speaker button (click or M to mute/unmute) and a volume slider next to Play. The slider only
  affects the preview, not the export.
- Buttons rearranged: Shortcuts (new keyboard icon) next to Project; Bitrate presets, Effects (magic wand) and
  Clear all under the preview. The Dark mode switch moved into the Export panel header, and the panel now runs
  from the top of the window.
- Effects window sections: Clip transitions (Transition effect), Speed up effects, Slow motion effects, Zoom
  effects.
- Fixed: section headers are blue again (the theme had turned them white).

0.9.13
- Export panel summary: clips and length, codec / resolution / crop, size limit or bitrate, and file name,
  separated by thin lines in a smaller font. The length now subtracts transition overlaps ("when joined").
- One Export button, which turns into a red Abort button while exporting.
- The status bar is gone. Export steps and results show in small text under the progress bar, and the bar
  itself says "Done in 3 minutes 53 seconds" (or Failed / Aborted). Open folder sits next to the bar.
- Editing messages (trim set, section added, ...) appear over the bottom of the preview for 3 seconds, then fade.
- "Presets" is now "Bitrate presets", next to Clear all under the preview. "Effects & settings" is now "Effect
  settings", in one column with App at the top. The clip count at the top is gone (it's in the summary).

0.9.12
- New layout: an Export panel on the right holds every export setting (size limit or fixed bitrate,
  resolution, codec, crop, HDR tone-map, audio bitrate and tracks, mute microphone, file name prefix/suffix,
  save folder), a summary (length after edits, size or estimated size, codec, example file name, save folder),
  the progress bar and the Export / Cancel buttons. It scrolls when the window is too short.
- New file name prefix (prefix_clip_suffix.mp4).
- The old Settings window is now "Effects & settings": clip effects, sped-up, slow-mo and zoom sections, app.
- The default window is wider (1500 px) to fit the panel; minimum width is 1150 px.

0.9.11
- New defaults: audio tracks mixed into one, sped-up volume 70%, slow-mo volume 150%, zoom sound 80%, zoom
  motion 0.4 s. Saved settings are kept; delete library\settings.json to get the new defaults. Double-clicking a
  volume slider resets it to its default.
- The Settings window is prepared in the background at start-up and fades in only once fully drawn.
- The transition hover preview is 25% larger.

0.9.10
- New "Glitch (digital)" transition: RGB split, jumping picture bands, noise and a flash while switching clips.
- Transition list cut to 22 (removed dissolve, grey fade, hard wipes, cover/reveal, open/close and squeeze).
- Play buttons next to the Sped-up, Slow-mo and Zoom volume sliders in Settings play a short sample (normal
  sound, the effect, then normal again) so you can judge the level. They use the selected clip's sound at the
  playhead, or a test melody when no clip with sound is loaded.
- Settings, Shortcuts and Presets open fully drawn with a dark title bar (no light flash in dark mode).

0.9.9
- 30 clip transitions, up from 6 (cut to 22 in 0.9.10): dissolve, fades through white or grey, wipes in 4
  directions, pushes up/down, circle open/close, clock wipe, diagonal, squeeze, zoom in, pixelize, blur and more.
- Hover over an entry in the Transition list (Settings > Clip effects) for a small looping preview. It uses
  your first two clips as they'd be joined, or plain colours when no clip is loaded.
- Deleting the selected clip now selects the next one (or the previous one if it was last), not the first.
- The total at the top includes speed-up and slow-mo sections, so it's the real length after edits.
- The status line shows how long the export took, e.g. "Export finished in 3 minutes 53 seconds".

0.9.8
- Default save folder (Settings > Export settings): when set, exports go there without asking, as
  name_suffix.mp4. If the name exists, it becomes "name (2).mp4"; nothing is overwritten. Empty means the
  program asks as before.
- Settings in two columns: Export settings (size, bitrate, resolution, codec, HDR tone-map, file name suffix,
  default save folder), Aspect ratio, Audio and App on the left; Clip effects and Sped-up, Slow-mo and Zoom
  sections on the right.
- New "Pitch" option for sped-up sections. "Speeds up with the video (high)" raises the pitch like a sped-up
  tape; "Stays the same (compressed)" is the old behaviour and the default.

0.9.7
- Rebindable shortcuts: in the Shortcuts window, click the key for set trim start/end, speed-up, slow-down or
  zoom, then press the new key, with Shift, Ctrl or Alt if you like (e.g. Shift + S). "Default" restores the
  original. The hints under the preview follow your choice.
- Settings > App: "File name suffix" (exports become name_suffix.mp4; empty uses the codec name, e.g.
  name_HEVC.mp4 or name_H264.mp4) and "Default save folder" (exports go there without asking).
- RIFE AI is the default slow-motion smoothing, and the transition length defaults to 0.4 s (new installs only;
  saved settings are kept). The label reads "Transition length (s)".
- Saving a project suggests the first clip's name.
- The AV1 export from 0.9.6 is removed again.

0.9.6
- Much smaller program: ffmpeg is a slim custom build with only the parts the program uses and no DLL files.
  The download shrank from 69 MB to about 27 MB (about 53 MB on disk with RIFE). RIFE slow-motion smoothing
  (library\rife, rife-v4.6 model, MIT license in library\rife\LICENSE.txt) is included, no download needed.
- Preview sound works with the slim ffmpeg.

0.9.5
- The experimental tracked zoom from 0.9.3 / 0.9.4 is removed; zoom sections work as in 0.9.2.
- "Download RIFE" fetches only what the program uses (the program, vcomp140.dll and the rife-v4.6 model, about
  12 MB instead of the 430 MB release zip) and shows the size and a progress bar. If a partial download isn't
  possible, it falls back to the whole zip. An old, big RIFE install still works; delete every folder in
  library\rife except rife-v4.6 to free about 400 MB.
- The launcher no longer requires the ffmpeg DLL files, so a slim ffmpeg.exe / ffprobe.exe in the library
  folder works.

0.9.2
- Zoom sections (hotkey Z, white, in a thin lane under the speed lane) zoom into part of the picture between two
  bars. Drag the white bracket on the preview to pick the area: inside to move, corners to resize. The bracket
  size sets the zoom level, up to 10x. Zoom sections can overlap speed and slow-motion sections. Their edges and
  bar snap to the playhead like other bars, and Delete or right-click removes one.
- Settings > ZOOM SECTIONS (third column): Motion (smooth zoom in/out, 0.5 s each by default, or an instant
  cut), motion length, Sound (a short whoosh when the zoom starts and ends) and its volume.
- The preview shows the zoom while playing; the bracket shows when paused.
- New hint under the preview: Z = zoom in (white, on a dark box in the light look so it stays readable).

0.9.0
- Snapping: drag a trim handle, or the edge or bar of a speed or slow-motion section, near the yellow playhead
  line (where you stopped playback) and it snaps to that exact spot. So: stop playback where you want the cut,
  then drag the handle next to the yellow line.

0.8.7
- Hints under the preview use the timeline colours: S = speed up (blue), D = slow down (pink). A down arrow
  points to "drag the divider below to resize".
- Settings: the heading is "SLOW-MO SECTIONS", with twice as much space between sections.
- Shortcuts window regrouped (General, Preview, Trimming, Speed & slow motion, Clips) with shorter descriptions
  and the same heading style as Settings.
- A little more space between the export row and the status bar; status text is one size smaller.

0.8.6
- Volume slider (0 to 200%) under the sound setting for sped-up and slow-motion sections. It applies to preview
  and export; double-click it to reset to 100%.
- "SLOW-MOTION SECTIONS" is now "SLOW-MO SECTIONS" in Settings; the preview hint says "D = slow down".
- The export progress bar has rounded corners and is exactly as tall as the buttons.
- The scroll bar next to the clips only appears when the clips don't fit.

0.8.5
- Rounder look: clip cards, their thumbnail strips and the dashed drop boxes have rounded corners.
- The Project menu is a roomy, borderless drop-down with rounded corners.
- Icons on the top buttons: key (Shortcuts), film strip (Presets), cog (Settings).
- "Sound" next to Play is now "Preview sound".
- The "Export settings" window is now just "Settings", in two roomier columns. Left: Size & quality, Picture,
  Clip join effects (was "Joining clips"), App. Right: Audio, Sped-up sections, Slow-motion sections.
- LICENSE.txt: Clip Shrinker is fully open source (MIT), so you can edit it, fork it and share it. Made with
  Claude (Anthropic) by Vergil.

0.8.2
- "Clear all" uses the theme's own rounded button style in red, matching the blue Export button.

0.8.1
- "Clear all" is a rounded red button again.

0.8.0 (bitrate presets, export question)
- New "Presets" button (left of Settings): bitrate profiles with a name, a bitrate in Mbps and an optional
  hotkey, saved in presets.json next to the program. Edit or X changes or deletes one; "+ Add profile" adds one.
- Every clip has a bitrate drop-down in its title bar: Auto (the size/bitrate from Settings) or a preset. A
  preset's hotkey applies it to the selected clips (or the active clip). The per-clip bitrate is used when clips
  are exported as separate files; a joined video follows the size/bitrate in Settings. The choice is saved in
  projects and covered by undo/redo.
- "Each clip as its own file / Join into one video" is no longer a setting: Export asks when there are several
  clips. Transition and length stay in Settings, since they only matter when joining.
- The progress bar is solid again (blue, green when finished). "Clear all" is red.
- Closing the program asks only: Save / Close without saving / Cancel.

0.7.6
- New 192k audio bitrate option (128k stays the default).
- New defaults for fresh installs: crop 16:9, join all clips into one video, transition "Gradient wipe, left to
  right". Your saved settings still win.

0.7.5
- New "Pitch" setting for slow-motion sound. "Slows down with the video (deep)" is classic tape-style slowdown
  (like Movie Studio's "classic" time stretch with the lock): slower and deeper, with no stretching artifacts.
  "Stays the same (stretched)" is the old behaviour. It applies to the slow-mo effect and normal slow-mo sound.
  The "Cut high notes" idea was dropped.

0.7.4
- The "Download RIFE" button hides once RIFE is installed.

0.7.2
- Progress bar stripes use the window's own grey (white in light mode) and run to both ends with no end caps.

0.7.1
- Slow-motion sections with "Slow-mo effect with sound" also get a deep, muffled sound.
- The progress bar is as tall as the buttons, shows the percentage in the middle, has darker stripes and turns
  green when the export finishes.
- The RIFE note in Settings is on its own line, so the window stays narrow.

0.7.0 (RIFE AI slow motion, export polish)
- Slow-motion sections can be smoothed with RIFE (AI frame interpolation, rife-ncnn-vulkan by nihui, MIT
  licence) under Settings > Slow-motion sections > Smoothing: Repeat frames / Frame blending / RIFE. The first
  time, click "Download RIFE" there (about 30 MB, once, into library\rife). If that fails, unzip the Windows
  release from github.com/nihui/rife-ncnn-vulkan/releases into library\rife yourself. It needs a Vulkan-capable
  graphics card (any recent NVIDIA card works).
- RIFE runs during export: the sections render first, and the bar shows "Slow motion (RIFE) 1/2 ...". The
  preview still uses frame blending. If RIFE is missing or fails, that section falls back to frame blending and
  the reason goes to clipshrinker.log.
- Temporary frames go in the Windows temp folder and are removed after the export. A 0.25x section of a long 4K
  clip needs a few GB free while it runs.
- "Export..." is now "Export", and Ctrl+E starts it.
- New striped progress bar, with "Open folder" to its right.
- The status line starts with a check mark when an export finishes and a cross when it's cancelled or fails.

0.6.0 (sound modes, bullet time, safer close)
- Settings has two new groups, "Sped-up sections" and "Slow-motion sections", each with a Sound drop-down:
  effect with sound / normal sound / mute. The VHS visual effect has its own checkbox.
- New deep "bullet time" sound for slow-motion sections: a sub thump and falling rumble at the start, a rising
  swell as it speeds back up at the end. The VHS sound is another 25% quieter.
- Closing with clips in the timeline asks first: save the project, close without saving, or keep working. With
  an empty timeline it just closes.
- Export no longer pops up a window. The usual finished sound plays, the result (including failed files) shows
  in the bottom bar, and an "Open folder" button appears next to Cancel and selects the saved file.

0.5.9 (slow-motion sections, VHS sound option)
- D adds a slow-motion section (pink, starting at 0.5x). It works like the blue speed section: type any
  multiplier below 1 (e.g. 0.25), or 1 or more to turn it blue.
- Slow-motion video blends neighbouring frames instead of repeating them (Settings > "Smooth slow-motion"). It
  isn't true interpolation, so very slow sections can look a bit ghosty. The sound is slowed with pitch kept.
- The VHS rewind effect now only applies to speed-up sections, and the tape sound has its own switch (Settings >
  "VHS rewind sound effect"). It's also 25% quieter.

0.5.8 (VHS rewind effect)
Sped-up sections get a VHS rewind look and sound, in preview and export:
- noise, colour bleed and a rolling tracking band while the section runs
- a stronger glitch burst and a rising tape-wind whoosh when the section starts, and a falling one when it
  returns to normal speed
- no effect on sections shorter than 0.15 s (after speeding up)
Toggle it in Settings > "VHS rewind effect on sped-up sections" (on by default, saved in projects).

0.5.7 (tidier top bar)
No 'Add videos' button: drop videos onto the window or click the drop zone (a slim strip below the clip list
once clips are loaded). 'Clear all' moved under the preview. Undo/redo are icon buttons (Ctrl+Z,
Ctrl+Shift+Z). The Shortcuts window is split into General / Preview / Timeline. New: M mutes/unmutes the
preview.

0.5.6 (undo / redo)
Undo/Redo buttons in the top bar, plus Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+Y (or Ctrl+Shift+Z), for removing, adding and
reordering clips, clear all, opening a project, trim markers, speed sections and their multipliers. Removed
clips stay hidden with their thumbnails, so undo brings them back instantly. The last 60 steps are kept.

0.5.5 (selecting clips)
Shift+click a clip's title line or strip to select everything between it and the active clip; Ctrl+click adds
or removes single clips; Ctrl+A selects all. Selected clips get the blue title bar like the active one. Delete
removes all selected clips (and the active one), or just the speed section if one is selected. A selected speed
section shows as a light cyan bar.

0.5.4 (projects)
Project button (top left), Ctrl+O, Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Shift+S open and save projects (*.clipproj) with the clips in
order, trim markers, speed sections and export settings. Dropping a project file on the window opens it. If a
clip has moved, the program also looks for it relative to the project file's folder.
Settings > APP > 'Restore the last session on start' (off by default) reopens the last session's clips.

0.5.3 (faster thumbnails)
A clip's thumbnails come from a single ffmpeg run (one quick key-frame seek per thumbnail) instead of one program
start per thumbnail. Up to 4 clips are processed at once, the active clip first, then the rest in list order.
Thumbnails appear one by one as they're ready.

0.5.2
Hotkeys 1 / 2 set the trim start/end marker at the playhead, while playing or scrubbing (markers can still be
dragged). While playing, a moved end marker takes effect immediately. The '?' button is now 'Shortcuts'.

0.5.1
While you drag a clip by its title line, a small card with its thumbnail and name follows the pointer. The
active clip's title bar is accent blue so it stands out from the thin strips.

0.5.0
Reorder clips by dragging their title line up or down (the arrow buttons are gone). Title line buttons are
bigger. Inactive clip strips show full-height trim markers and speed sections, without the playhead.

0.4.9 (was 4.8)
Version numbers changed to 0.x while the tool is in development; the earlier 4.x versions correspond to 0.4.x.
The title line buttons (Fit, up, down, remove) are flat and borderless, matching the card colour with no
rounded corners sticking out. They highlight on hover; the remove button is red.

4.7 (clip card tidy-up)
No more white lines across the timelines. Smaller title, buttons and info text. Clicking a clip's title line
selects it. The remove button is red and set apart from the arrows.

4.6 (compact clip strips)
Only the active clip shows its full timeline; the others are thin strips (title, trim handles, speed sections),
so many clips fit without much scrolling. Click a strip to make it active: it expands, the playhead jumps to the
clicked point, and the list scrolls to keep it visible.

4.5 (settings window)
All export settings moved into their own window (Settings button or F2), so the preview gets the whole upper area
and the clip list more room. Changes apply and save immediately, and the bottom bar summarises the current
settings (size/bitrate, codec, crop, join).

4.3 / 4.4 (smoother preview for 4K clips)
Playing from any point shows the picture immediately. Preview audio streams continuously (no temporary files,
gaps or dropouts) and starts exactly with the first frame. Preview decoding and downscaling run on the GPU when
possible (no crop, HDR tone-mapping or speed sections active), with an automatic fallback if the GPU path isn't
available. Preview timings go to clipshrinker.log in the library folder, which helps if anything still feels
slow.
